findings.title: Unconfirmed-run faults are not kept open between polls
findings.description: After an unconfirmed launch’s poll fails, `_fault` records the fault, but the next tick can reach the “poll not due” branch and return without replaying it unless the launch was already marked overdue. The same can happen to a log-read fault from `_check_line`, which is not retained for replay. `ProjectTick` then sees no recurring fault and may close the escalation even though the run is still unconfirmed and its observation problem has not recovered. Replay standing faults on the unconfirmed path as well.

findings.title: The project view is only shallowly frozen
findings.description: `ProjectView` is a frozen dataclass, but `link_probes` is passed a mutable `dict` from `LinkProbes.results`. A planner can mutate that mapping, so later planners in `decide` may see a different view than earlier planners. This breaks the documented frozen-view and deterministic-planning contract. Pass an immutable copy or otherwise prevent mutation of the mapping.

findings.title: Add a Runner load test for the process path
findings.description: The Runner adds tick scheduling and subprocess activity, including polling children and processing multiple projects. The added tests exercise unit, end-to-end, and crash-recovery behavior, but there is no Runner-focused load test in `tests/load/` asserting latency, throughput, or resource bounds. The Python testing rules require a CI-gated load test for code on process/concurrency paths.
